problem:
Which of the following integrals evaluates to zero due to symmetry?

- ${\int }_{-1/2}^{1/2}{x}^{2}\operatorname{sin}⁡x\,\text{d}x$
- ${\int }_{-\pi /8}^{\pi /8}\frac{{x}^{4}+2}{3}\,\text{d}x$
- ${\int }_{-3}^{3}({e}^{x}-{e}^{-x})\,\text{d}x$

feedback.problem:
Which of the following integrals evaluates to zero due to symmetry?

- ${\int }_{-5}^{5}x\operatorname{cos}⁡({x}^{2})\,\text{d}x$
- ${\int }_{-2}^{2}x\operatorname{sin}⁡(x+1)\,\text{d}x$
- ${\int }_{-\pi }^{\pi }({x}^{3}-2x)\,\text{d}x$
feedback.worked_solution:
Recall the following:

- a function $f(x)$ is *even* if $f(-x)=f(x)$

- a function $f(x)$ is *odd* if $f(-x)=-f(x)$

Moreover, for any odd function $f(x),$ the graph of $y=f(x)$ has rotational symmetry of order $2$ about the origin, so we have

$$
{\int }_{-a}^{a}f(x)\,\text{d}x=0.
$$

So, to determine which integrals evaluate to zero due to symmetry, we have to determine which integrands are odd functions.

- The function $f(x)=x\operatorname{cos}⁡({x}^{2})$ is an odd function:

$$
\begin{aligned}f(-x) & =(-x)\operatorname{cos}⁡((-x)^{2}) \\  & =-x\operatorname{cos}⁡({x}^{2}) \\  & =-f(x)\,✓\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, by symmetry, we can conclude that

$$
{\int }_{-5}^{5}x\operatorname{cos}⁡({x}^{2})\,\text{d}x=0.
$$

- The function $g(x)=x\operatorname{sin}⁡(x+1)$ is *not* an odd function:

$$
\begin{aligned}g(-x) & =(-x)\operatorname{sin}⁡(-x+1) \\  & =-x\operatorname{sin}⁡(1-x) \\  & \ne -g(x)\,\times \end{aligned}
$$

- The function $h(x)={x}^{3}-2x$ is an odd function:

$$
\begin{aligned}h(-x) & =(-x)^{3}-2(-x) \\  & =-{x}^{3}+2x \\  & =-({x}^{3}-2x) \\  & =-h(x)\,✓\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, by symmetry, we can conclude that

$$
{\int }_{-\pi }^{\pi }({x}^{3}-2x)\,\text{d}x=0.
$$

Therefore, the correct answer is "I and III only."
